item.title: Friday scent of the day 8/14
item.dc:creator: Robin
item.description:
Happy Friday and happy National Creamsicle Day!  Our community project for today: wear a creamsicle fragrance, if you have one. (And you can find lots of suggestions — including layering combos — in the comments to 5 perfumes: consider the creamsicle). This is a repeat from 2020. 

What fragrance did you pick? As always, do chime in with your scent of the day even if you’re not participating in the community project.

I completely failed...I tried a layering combination of DIY Sweet Orange Lotion, Hermès Elixir des Merveilles and Maya Njie Vanilj, which I thought might produce something like a creamsicle cookie, but nope, no creamsicle whatsoever...

item.title: Positive scent memories from early life
item.dc:creator: Robin
item.description: A recent study in PLOS Biology explored how positive scent memories from early life form, survive, and change inside the brain. Through a human survey and a series of mouse experiments, the study traces these memories from their first roots in the olfactory bulb to the wider networks that carry their emotional meaning later in […]
item.content:encoded:
A recent study in PLOS Biology explored how positive scent memories from early life form, survive, and change inside the brain. Through a human survey and a series of mouse experiments, the study traces these memories from their first roots in the olfactory bulb to the wider networks that carry their emotional meaning later in life.

— Read more in How the Scent of Childhood Takes Root in the Brain at Psychology Today.

item.title: Partly practical
item.dc:creator: Robin
item.description: For Oswaldo Maciá, a pioneer in the field of olfactory art, the appeal of using scent is partly practical. “I don’t know how many biennales I have done, but you will have hundreds of people passing in front of your work. They won’t watch a half-hour video or listen to a three-minute piece. Smell is the only language that can instantly […]
item.content:encoded:
For Oswaldo Maciá, a pioneer in the field of olfactory art, the appeal of using scent is partly practical. “I don’t know how many biennales I have done, but you will have hundreds of people passing in front of your work. They won’t watch a half-hour video or listen to a three-minute piece. Smell is the only language that can instantly hit the brain.”  

— Read more in Follow Your Nose: From provocative perfumes to show‑specific scents, olfactory art is moving into the mainstream at Ocula.

item.title: The daily lemming
item.dc:creator: Robin
item.description: From Luna Nectar, Nocturne Magnesium Sleep Oil: "Nocturne is a topical magnesium oil that supports sleep and relaxation. Compared to conventional magnesium sprays that may cause itchiness or stinging, our formula is infused with aloe vera to diminish such side effects, and calming lavender to induce relaxation." $39 for 100 ml at Ulta.
